items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1958-05-31
items.q: There's two in New York that learned under Dio. Orma Simeone and Albert Dix today.

ctx.x: Barney is your cousin. My cousin.

One job with Barney. He was busy, I was busy. The only one who had that after hour dance, you see. At the Sherman Hotel. I'll never forget that. That's why I worked with Barney. And Albert Dix was too. Wasn't that one learned under Lorenzo Dio. He's in New York. There's two in New York that learned under Dio. Orma Simeone and Albert Dix today. Good clarinet.
Can you tell us about Jimmy Brown? Jimmy Brown bass violin.

items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1967-11-15
items.q: that's who taught Bonnet de God and had your dad in charge with you.

ctx.x: So, he died. They buried his planet with him. His planet, his planet, his planet,

his planet, his planet, his planet. And they had another one, Lorenzo Teo. An old man, Teo. I'm gonna tell you, your dad, if you at least tell you. You know where you used to go out? On the wagon. And he started playing that jazz music. He'd run in there. He'd run in there. I'd say, please let me get under your bed. You know, he jazz. What a musician. You could sit right here. And he started playing that claddle. He'd take me two blocks away. Old man watching that. His son, his son, Lorenzo was the planet. Well,…
